confidence: high for mathematical constraints; moderate for search priorities

exactConstraint.target: total > 92 if and only if L+d < 8
exactConstraint.strictBoundary: A ceiling equal to 92 does not qualify.
necessaryConditions: Both thematic deductions must be zero. Either -10 deduction alone makes the target impossible.
A verified Amazon count below 100 makes the target impossible, because its deduction is at least 10.
With 100-999 Amazon ratings, publication-age plus history-age loss must be strictly below 3; all quality loss must fit inside what remains.
With at least 1000 Amazon ratings, publication-age plus history-age loss must be strictly below 8; all quality loss must fit inside what remains.
For H13=0, 100-999 ratings requires an original year later than 1996 even at perfect positive attainment. At least 1000 ratings requires an original year later than 1946.
An unknown Amazon count receives the prescribed zero fallback after attempts, but unknown is not evidence that the book is popular. Do not select inaccessible counts to evade the rule.
exactConstraint.criterionBound: For remaining quality-loss budget B=8-d, each quadratic criterion must independently satisfy x>sqrt(m*(m-B)) when 0<B<m. Each linear criterion must satisfy x>m-B. These are necessary, not sufficient; the losses also have to sum to less than B.

examples.conclusion: Cannot exceed 92 even with every other criterion perfect and no deductions.
Cannot exceed 92 even before publication age and all other quality losses.

examples.condition: E=19, 100-999 Amazon ratings, original year 2015 or earlier
examples.conclusion: Cannot exceed 92 even if every other criterion is perfect and H13=0.

examples.condition: 2020 original publication, H13=0, at least1000 ratings

heuristicFilters: Search first among explanatory technology, production, materials, computing, logistics and innovation books first published since 2006. This is a priority window, not an exclusion rule.
Prefer a verified Amazon aggregate of at least 1000, because eliminating the five-point penalty usually matters more than small differences in public star ratings.
Prefer broad cross-period or present-system explanations. A bounded historical case can still qualify, but its exact endpoint consumes the same eight-point loss budget.
Look for both detailed specialist approval and specific negative reviews. A string of generic recommendations does not establish evidence integrity or causal depth.
Use Goodreads, StoryGraph and LibraryThing ratings to find reader reception and repeated complaints; do not translate their counts into Amazon counts or their stars into the rubric score.

Select a short complete thread with a narrow industrial or systems question before a very large generic best-books thread. Once a source is adopted, account for every title in its accessible main content and comments.

Look for concrete discussion of bottlenecks, production scale, complementary inputs, process reliability, adoption constraints and substitution. These offer better topic-fit signals than the word technology alone.

Use source yields only after measuring them: unique eligible titles, mathematical ceiling survivors, fully evidenced assessments and research time. No numerical success probabilities are justified by the present data.

calibrationAudit.interpretation: No E20 or D10 occurs in the current data. The most recent39 assessments also use mostly integer values around E17-18 and D8-9. This suggests compressed scale use worth auditing; it does not prove any individual score is wrong or authorize an uplift.
rubricRisks: Evidence integrity does not require a controlled experiment or a fully quantified causal model for every historical narrative.
Authority can come from access, practice or unusual synthesis; being a journalist is not an automatic cap.
Density measures whether length is earned. Difficulty or slow reading belongs primarily under clarity, unless the difficulty is caused by unnecessary material.
Each raised score needs a specific corrected rationale or new evidence. A target shortfall is not evidence.
The same identified flaw should not silently be charged to several criteria unless it has a distinct effect on each.

sourceAdvice.verifiedCapability: The official API exposes child comment IDs and thread descendant counts.
sourceAdvice.use: Find narrow Ask HN threads on manufacturing, infrastructure, industrial history and systems. Traverse the comment tree, record missing/dead items, and inspect disagreement.
sourceAdvice.limitation: Votes and repeated mentions are discovery signals, not independent factual verification.

sourceAdvice.verifiedCapability: The founder's feature announcement describes tag, date and author filters, including custom date ranges.
sourceAdvice.use: Seed with known good books; combine technology/industrial-history tags and a recent original-publication range; diversify authors.
sourceAdvice.limitation: The announcement warns publication dates can be imperfect. Recommendation similarity is not a quality score. Current direct page returned a high-load redirect, but the indexed official announcement was accessible.

sourceAdvice.verifiedCapability: Official site describes mood, pace, fiction/nonfiction and genre filters, custom tags and lists, and fractional reader ratings.
sourceAdvice.use: Check recurring complaints about repetition, weak structure or shallow content; use nonfiction and subject filters for discovery.
sourceAdvice.limitation: Mood fit and aggregate enjoyment do not demonstrate factual reliability or specialist depth.

sourceAdvice.verifiedCapability: Its database admits books after at least three outlet reviews, assigns four categories and weights accepted reviews equally.
sourceAdvice.use: Open the mixed and negative reviews as well as positive ones. Follow links to the original review, especially to identify concrete objections.
sourceAdvice.limitation: Its method normally considers reviews within three months of publication; this can miss later corrections. Literary reviewers have different expertise. The aggregate is not a scientific validation.

sourceAdvice.verifiedCapability: The site interviews experts about five selected books and their reasons.
sourceAdvice.use: Search expert interviews on technology, economic history, engineering and industrial change. Explanations are more useful than a bare list.
sourceAdvice.limitation: A specialist can nominate textbooks, old works or narrow books that fail this repository's rules. The interviewer's selection is not independent replication.

sourceAdvice.verifiedCapability: The Royal Society maintains popular science prize shortlists and judging information.
sourceAdvice.use: Use shortlists as one discovery pool, then apply the reader's topic and technical-depth filters.
sourceAdvice.limitation: Many excellent popular science books are introductory physics, disease or environment books and therefore poor fits here.
